subject: Help with interpretation of a mediation model with blavaan

messages.author: 96688ca0745f2f4d
messages.subject: Help with interpretation of a mediation model with blavaan
parts:
Hi all,

I am excited that blavaan started to return something in my models in latest development version. I have three questions below.

The model looks like:

total <- "vol =~  lh_parahippocampal_area+lh_entorhinal_area
        +lh_transversetemporal_area+rh_temporalpole_area
+lh_frontalpole_area+rh_frontalpole_area

sch =~ z_pos_2grp+ z_neg_2grp+ z_dis_2grp

bio =~ BDNFord + EGFRord + IL3ord +FGFord + COMTord

sch ~ c*bio

vol ~ a*bio

sch ~ b*vol

ab := a*b
totalaz := c+(a*b)
"

The output of the analysis:

> fit <- bsem(total, data = subjcharac)
Compiling rjags model...
Calling the simulation using the rjags method...
Adapting the model for 1000 iterations...
  |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++| 100%
Burning in the model for 4000 iterations...
  |**************************************************| 100%
Running the model for 10000 iterations...
  |**************************************************| 100%
Simulation complete
Calculating summary statistics...
Note: The monitored variables 'lambda[1,1,1]', 'lambda[7,2,1]',
'lambda[10,3,1]', 'alpha[1,1,1]', 'alpha[2,1,1]' and 'alpha[3,1,1]' appear
to be non-stochastic; they will not be included in the convergence
diagnostic
Calculating the Gelman-Rubin statistic for 53 variables....
Finished running the simulation
Computing posterior predictives...
> summary(fit)
Error in if (object@Fit@iterations > 0) { : 
  argumento tem comprimento zero
> fitMeasures(fit)
      npar       logl        ppp        bic        dic      p_dic       waic 
    45.000   -252.978      0.000    695.834    572.350     33.197    566.731 
    p_waic      looic      p_loo margloglik 
    26.453    566.919     26.547   -637.247 
Warning messages:
1: 22 (31.9%) p_waic estimates greater than 0.4.
We recommend trying loo() instead. 
2: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are slightly high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.

My questions:

  • It does not show an error indicating that the model did not converge, but summary(fit) does not work. Is it a bug? The fitMeasures function works fine.
  • a low ppp means a bad model, right?
  • blavaan does not handle missing values, and should fiter them out first, am I right?

Thank you for any help,

Luis

​

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Help with interpretation of a mediation model with blavaan
parts:
Luis

The error of the summary function may be related to a bug that is fix in the development version, try to explicitly set the burnin and sample, like
bsem(total, data = subjcharac, adapt=1000, burnin=5000, sample=4000)

The ppp is (for now) the only measure of absolute fit, BUT is not reliable, it is very easy for it to find a model to have bad fit. Think of it similar to the p-value of the chisquare in the frequentist SEM. For now I would recommend you to look at the fit in function of the parameters, are the standardized factor loadings large, factor correlation make theoretical sense, etc

About missing data, blvaan does handle missing data , it handles it as JAGS handles missing data as default. With data augmentation, at each iteration values are imputed into the missing values, the imputations are drawn from the posterior distribution conditional on the model parameters. So, missing values are both parameters and data

Hope this helps
